record.paper_title: Quadratic Stochastic Operators: Results and Open Problems
record.original_question: For a transversal Volterra quadratic stochastic operator, the fixed-point set X in S^{m-1} is finite. Choose neighborhoods U_1, ..., U_t of the fixed points x_1, ..., x_t, and for a trajectory x^{(0)}, x^{(1)}, ... record its itinerary as the sequence n_1, n_2, ... of fixed-point neighborhoods visited successively. Does there exist a trajectory of a transversal Volterra QSO whose itinerary is periodic?

evidence.quote: Thus the trajectory firstly visits the neighborhood of a fixed point xn1 then it visits the neighborhood of a fixed point xn2 and so on. The sequence n1 , n2 , ... is called the itinerary (route-march) of the trajectory x(0) , x(1) , ...
Problem 3. Is there a trajectory with periodic itinerary?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S^{m-1}=\{x=(x_1,\dots,x_m)\in\mathbb{R}^m: x_i\ge 0,\ \sum_{i=1}^m x_i=1\}$ be the $(m-1)$-dimensional simplex. A quadratic stochastic operator (QSO) $V:S^{m-1}\to S^{m-1}$ is defined by
$$(Vx)_k=\sum_{i,j=1}^m p_{ij,k}\, x_i x_j,\qquad k=1,\dots,m,$$
where the coefficients satisfy $p_{ij,k}=p_{ji,k}\ge 0$ and $\sum_{k=1}^m p_{ij,k}=1$ for all $i,j$. The operator $V$ is called a Volterra QSO if $p_{ij,k}=0$ whenever $k\notin\{i,j\}$. A Volterra QSO is called transversal if, in addition, its fixed-point set $X\subset S^{m-1}$ is finite; write $X=\{x_1,\dots,x_t\}$.

Choose pairwise disjoint open neighborhoods $U_1,\dots,U_t$ of $x_1,\dots,x_t$ in $S^{m-1}$. For an initial point $x^{(0)}\in S^{m-1}$, consider the trajectory $x^{(n+1)}=V(x^{(n)})$, $n\ge 0$. Suppose there is an infinite sequence of indices $0\le k_1<k_2<\cdots$ and indices $n_1,n_2,\dots\in\{1,\dots,t\}$ such that $x^{(k_r)}\in U_{n_r}$ for every $r$, and that this records each successive visit of the trajectory to the chosen neighborhoods; the sequence $n_1,n_2,\dots$ is called the itinerary of $x^{(0)}$.

Question: Does there exist a transversal Volterra QSO $V$ on some simplex $S^{m-1}$ and an initial point $x^{(0)}\in S^{m-1}$ whose itinerary $(n_r)_{r\ge 1}$ is periodic (i.e. there exists $T\ge 1$ with $n_{r+T}=n_r$ for all $r\ge 1$)?
artifact.status_search_result: Web search shows ongoing study of trajectories of Volterra and ℓ-Volterra QSOs, with results stating that standard Volterra QSOs admit no periodic trajectories while ℓ-Volterra QSOs may have periodic orbits. However, the specific question of whether a transversal Volterra QSO can produce a periodic itinerary (sequence of visited fixed-point neighborhoods) was not found to be definitively settled in the available sources.

status_evidence.claim: Related results on periodic points of ℓ-Volterra QSOs; no explicit resolution of the transversal Volterra itinerary problem.

status_evidence.title: On a Superposition of Volterra and Permuted Volterra QSOs
status_evidence.snippet: studies of permuted Volterra quadratic stochastic operators identified cases with 5-periodic orbits
